newsitem.title: GERMANY: MBT buy to boost SKW Trostberg debt.
newsitem.headline: MBT buy to boost SKW Trostberg debt.

text.p: The acquisition of Swiss group Master Builders Technologies will leave German specialty chemicals group SKW Trostberg AG with debts of around two billion marks, the group said on Wednesday.
SKW Trostberg will officially take over MBT from Swiss chemicals group Sandoz AG before the end of the year and will then become the world's leading construction chemicals group.

MBT will officially cost SKW Trostberg 1.3 billion Swiss francs and SKW will pay 1.1 billion Swiss francs in cash and acquire 200 million Swiss francs in debt, chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schulz told a news conference.

"Our debt will therefore be about two billion marks," Schulz said, adding that this sum would first need to be digested before the group reviews possible future acquisition plans. SKW Trostberg has posted strong gains recently, fueled in particular by acquistions like the takeover of SBI from French group Sanofi SA.
About half of the cost of MBT will be attributed to good will which is to be written off over the next 15 years, the group said.

SKW Trostberg, which floated shares last spring, will not raise capital to finance the takeover but rather borrow from banks in a variety of currencies, including yen, dollars, marks, and Swiss francs, Schulz said.
In total the interest payment rates will be around five percent, making it more attractive to finance the deal with loans rather than through a capital hike, Schulz added.
The integration of MBT will be relatively quick SKW Trostberg officials added, noting that the acquisition will already make a positive contribution to results next year.
Even though goodwill, expected to be 52 million marks next year will weigh on the 1997 net profit, Schulz predicted that earnings per share will benefit from the takeover.
"The synergies will already be visible next year," Schulz said.
